items.title: 67460_Sammy Price oral history interview
items.q: I wish I knew what Billy Taylor did, or how he could do it. And I'm calling his name because I have a great respect for him and he's accomplished things.

ctx.x: So Billy Rose wasn't at the Diamond Horseshoe. They asked me to come over to his house on Sutton Place. So I went over to Billy's house and we became like father and son, or brother...two brothers. So he says, "Sam, now I'll tell you. I don't care what happens, you got the job." He wanted two piano players. "You got one of the jobs. Don't worry." He said, "No matter what you see me do, or what I do, don't you worry." Do you know that he called at least a hundred piano players to play with me? James P. Johnson,…
Billy was...oh, he was some showman. 'Course, wait 'til I tell you what Tallulah Bankhead did to him. He wanted untrained sound. He wanted it to be primitive,

and this is what I was playing. But he wanted that other piano player to be able to play with me, which would show a contrast, yet it would be similar, or it could work together. So here we come...we tried everybody...James P.--I thought James P. was going to get it. And Willie 'the Lion,' I thought he was going to get it...I thought they was going to go by the name of a person, you know, but they finally ended up selecting Arthur Gibbs, the man that wrote "Running Wild."
